title: token-rotation-mechanism
intention: A token posted on the cairn device's announce feed rotates through every device in alpha order — each device's probe fires, runs its sleep cycle or forwards, and the rotation completes back to start.
why: One token rotation replaces N independent sleep daemons — the same move the ground loop made for heartbeats. Serial by design because of measured OOM history (n=3) and because we don't yet know which sleep cycles are independent. The probe pattern is the mechanism: a three-line custom probe (match, decide, forward) is a valid implementation; no shim overhead, no bus routing, no LLM needed (Akien, 2026-08-24).
traces_to: Telos aim 5 (self-improving) — the rotation gives each device its maintenance window
Law 4 — the token on the bus is physics: a device's probe fires because a message arrived, not a schedule
Shrinking-footprint derivation — one token rotation vs N independent daemons

proves_green.proof_gate: tester — a token posted on the announce feed rotates through at least one device and returns, proved by teeth a hollow build could not pass

falsifier.proves_red: DONE when a token can be posted, received by at least one device, forwarded through the roster, and return to the cairn device with at least one real sleep cycle executed. WRONG INTENT if the rotation mechanism is the wrong shape — e.g., devices need to sleep concurrently, or the bus is the wrong transport.
falsifier.horizon: first complete rotation is the first measurement

how: The cairn device posts a sleep-cycle token on its announce feed. Each device has a three-line probe that matches the token, checks whether it is that device's turn in alpha order (from the ground loop's roster), runs its sleep cycle if it is, and forwards the token to the next device. The last device forwards back to the cairn device, completing the rotation.

decisions.text: PLACEMENT. The rotation mechanism is a NEW MACHINE of the cairn device at cairn/devices/cairn/machines/sleep_cycle/ — `__init__.py` (empty), `intention+why.json` (runtime_role "machine", keyed like cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/intention+why.json: component, runtime_role, role, schema_version, what, why, invoke, node_class, entry, state_and_history, filed_edges, gates, falsifier, how_it_learns, traces_to, owner, gated_by, gated_by_why, proof, provenance, learns, claim_provenance), `token.py` (the whole mechanism), `proofs/test_token_rotation.py`. NOTHING berths under cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/ (ground loop = heartbeat + device list, Akien CC-- x4); the 2026-09-06 decompose berth's writes_to under ground_loop/sleep_cycle.py is superseded by the re-berthed stages 4–7 of 2026-09-18 that claim this ticket. The device-side helper is a base tool at cairn/tools/base/mail_probe.py (D5) and the cairn device's verbs land in cairn/devices/cairn/device.py (D2).

SHAPE: HUB, NOT RELAY — measured. `Probe.to` is a static field (cairn/tools/base/probe.py, the Probe dataclass; shim.py:545 posts to `cb.to` verbatim) and a probe may not import the cairn device's roster (no cross-device imports), so a device's three-line probe CANNOT address 'the next device'. Therefore the cairn device HANDS the token to each device in turn and every device answers back to cairn, which hands to the next: (a) `token.mint(bus, *, roots=None, roster_root=None, now=None)` opens a cycle {cycle_id: uuid hex, roster: D3, position: 0, visited: [], opened_at, closed_at: None, closed_by: None}, writes it (D4) and hands to roster[0]; (b) a HAND is `bus.post(sender="cairn", to=<device>, channel="personal", verb="", why="sleep token", body={"sleep_token": cycle_id, "position": i, "of": n})` — verb-less BECAUSE a verbed envelope to a discovered device bounces (shim.deliver: `_FeedbackDevice` declares no verbs) while a verb-less one lands in its inbound DataRecorder via receive(); (c) the device's probe answers by poking `to="cairn", verb="sleep-token", channel="personal"`, body={"sleep_token": cycle_id, "device": <id>, "answer": <what its sleep work returned>}; (d) CairnDevice.declared_verbs() grows `sleep-token` → `_handle_sleep_token(envelope)` = `token.receive_answer(bus, envelope["body"], roots=..., now=...)`: an answer whose sleep_token != the standing open cycle_id, or from a device that is not roster[position], is REFUSED loudly — emit `sleep_token_refused`, return {"accepted": False, "reason": ...}, cycle untouched; an accepted answer appends {device, answer, at} to visited, advances position, and either hands to the next device or CLOSES the cycle (closed_at, closed_by="rotation complete"); returns {"accepted": True, "cycle_id": ..., "position": ..., "closed": bool}. HANDLER RESULTS NEVER CARRY THE KEY `sleep_token` (the shim posts the result back to the device as a reply, which lands in the same inbound recorder the probe reads — D5 matches on that key). (e) a second verb `sleep-cycle` → `_handle_sleep_cycle(envelope)` with body {"act": "mint"} (= mint) or {"act": "show"} (= the standing cycle.json, or {"cycle": None}). (f) THE ANNOUNCE FEED IS THE RECORD OF THE ROTATION: every hand and the close each post ONE record `bus.post(sender="cairn", to="cairn", channel="announce", why="sleep token", verb="", body={"cycle_id", "event": "hand"|"closed", "device", "position", "of"})` — announce has no delivery (bus.py: delivery only on personal), so it is a record, never a transport; a complete rotation over n devices leaves exactly n+1 announce records for that cycle_id. AS SETTLED IN PASS 1 (folded so this step reads whole) — In receive_answer(), after appending the visit and incrementing position, the cycle CLOSES when position == len(roster) (closed_by "rotation complete", one announce record with event "closed"); otherwise it HANDS to roster[position] (one announce record with event "hand"). So n devices leave exactly n+1 announce records for the cycle_id.

ROSTER. `token.roster(root=None) -> list[str]`: alpha-sorted, de-duplicated device ids from `cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop.discovery.device_folders(root)` (the ground loop's own roster, read from disk every time — never cached), FILTERED to folders that hold the file `token.SLEEP_PROBE == "sleeps_when_the_token_arrives.py"`. Opt-in by file, measured 2026-09-18: device_folders() returned 43 probes folders and 0 of them carry a sleep probe, so an unfiltered token would be handed to a device with nothing to answer it and the rotation would stall at position 0 forever. A device joins the rotation by berthing that one file in its probes/ folder (D5 makes it three lines) and leaves it by deleting the file — the same physics as the ground loop's roster. An EMPTY roster closes the cycle at mint with closed_by="nothing to visit" and one announce record (event "closed", of=0).

STATE. The standing cycle lives in instance-space at `instance_path("cairn", 0, roots) / "machines" / "sleep_cycle" / "cycle.json"` (cairn.tools.base.address.instance_path; roots=None is the live ~/.cairn) — the whole dict of D2(a), rewritten atomically (write to cycle.json.tmp then os.replace) on every change. `token.standing(roots=None) -> dict | None` reads it. mint() while a cycle is OPEN supersedes it: the open cycle is appended as one line to `superseded.jsonl` beside cycle.json with superseded_at, then the new cycle replaces it (Law 7: the old record is kept, corrected by a later line). Closed cycles stay in cycle.json until the next mint. No runtime state in the repo.

DEVICE-SIDE HELPER: cairn/tools/base/mail_probe.py, `answers_mail(key, handle, *, device_file, why, to="cairn", verb="", horizon=1000) -> Probe`. device_id = Path(device_file).resolve().parent.parent.name (the probes/ folder's parent — the same rule discovery.device_folders uses). Inbound = DataRecorder(instance_path(device_id, 0, roots) / "tools" / "data_recorder" / "inbound") — exactly where `_FeedbackDevice.receive` (ground_loop/discovered.py) lands a discovered device's mail — with roots = context.get("roots") (None live; a proof hands fixture roots in the beat context). Answered = DataRecorder(... / "tools" / "data_recorder" / "answered"). PENDING = inbound records whose body is a dict carrying `key` and whose envelope_id is not in the answered recorder's envelope_ids, in write order. trigger(now, context) is true iff pending is non-empty; the survey is memoised with probe.once(context, f"mail_probe:{device_id}:{key}", ...) — keyed by device because the beat's context is SHARED across every shim. carry(context) takes the OLDEST pending record, calls `handle(body) -> answer` (the device's sleep work, whatever it is), writes an answered record {finding: f"answered {key}", inspector_target: device_id, probe_source: "mail_probe", envelope_id, answer} and returns the poke body {key: body[key], "device": device_id, "answer": answer}. enough never (a mailbox never retires). while_true=True so two tokens in one beat are answered on consecutive beats instead of the second waiting for the trigger to fall. A device's sleep probe is then three lines: `from cairn.tools.base.mail_probe import answers_mail` / `def _sleep(body): return <its work>` / `PROBE = answers_mail("sleep_token", _sleep, device_file=__file__, why="...", verb="sleep-token")`. The base charter cairn/tools/base/intention+why.json gets ONE added invoke line naming mail_probe (its `what` enumerates the modules) and recompile_gate.sh runs in the same act.

BOUNDS. constrain-20260906T105321-ac8cedd9d817 puts 'what sleep work is' OUT, so NO LIVE DEVICE gets a sleeps_when_the_token_arrives.py in this ticket — the live roster is empty after this build and a live mint closes as "nothing to visit". The falsifier's 'at least one real sleep cycle executed' is met INSIDE THE PROOF: three fixture devices each do measurable work in handle() (each writes one record to its own fixture recorder and returns it), and the proof asserts the work happened in roster order. Fixture: a tmp root with devices/fx_sleep_a, fx_sleep_b, fx_sleep_c each holding probes/sleeps_when_the_token_arrives.py written as the D5 three-liner; fixture roots {"repo": <tmp>, "commons": <tmp>, "instance": <tmp>/instance}; the probes are imported with discovery.load_module and driven by GroundLoopDevice(bus=bus) beats through hand-held shims (BaseShim subclasses with _presence=ONLINE whose _start_device returns a mailbox that records inbound mail at instance_path(id, 0, fixture_roots)/tools/data_recorder/inbound with the same keys _FeedbackDevice.receive writes; probes() returns the loaded PROBE); the cairn side is CairnShim-shaped with CairnDevice(bus=bus, roots=fixture_roots, roster_root=<tmp>); beat context carries {"roots": fixture_roots}. PROVES["bf146e9e3967"] = ONE composite tooth (the falsifier is unnumbered → clause "all", per proof_coverage) that prints green on green and asserts: (1) roster(<tmp>) == [a, b, c]; (2) after mint + enough beats the cycle is closed with visited devices in exactly that order and each device's fixture recorder holds its one work record; (3) at every point at most one device holds an unanswered token; (4) exactly 4 announce records for the cycle_id (3 hands + 1 close); (5) an answer carrying a stale cycle_id is refused with accepted False and leaves the cycle untouched; (6) an empty roster closes at mint with "nothing to visit". Subjects imported INSIDE the tooth (hollow UNRAN otherwise). Run twice; check pc.clauses/pc.lacks before the first seal.
